title: fix(spec): $like / $ilike `_` is one Unicode code point on every JS face
body:
Fixes #20143

Clause-②: yes

## What was wrong

`$like` / `$ilike` answered two different row sets for one filter, depending on the driver behind the object. The SQLite faces (`driver-sql` on better-sqlite3, `driver-sqlite-wasm`, `driver-turso` local and remote) compile `_` to GLOB's `?` through `likePatternToGlobPattern`, and `?` counts **code points**. The JavaScript faces compiled the spec's `likePatternToRegexSource` with **no regex flags**, so `_` → `[\s\S]` read one **UTF-16 code unit**, which is half of an emoji. The spec's text said "`_` matches exactly one character" without saying which unit.

Triage set the direction: `_` is one code point. The stop condition (a real semantic reason for the UTF-16 reading) was measured and does not hold; see below.

## The fix

- **`@objectstack/spec`** (`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`)
  - New export `likePatternToRegExp(pattern, foldAscii = false): RegExp`. It compiles `likePatternToRegexSource` with the `u` flag and nothing else, so the flag lives in the one shared definition instead of in each consumer.
  - `matchesLikePattern` now evaluates `likePatternToRegExp`.
  - `likePatternToRegexSource` is **unchanged** and still exported. Its docblock gains a section saying the source means one code point per `_` only under `u`.
  - `LIKE_DESCRIPTION` and the GLOB table now say which "character" is meant.
- **`@objectstack/driver-memory`** (`src/memory-driver.ts`): both mingo doors (the `$like` filter at `normalizeFilterCondition`, and the AST `like` / `ilike` node at `convertConditionToMongo`) built their own `new RegExp(likePatternToRegexSource(...))` with no flags. They now take `likePatternToRegExp`. **This is a source change outside the claim's expected surface.** Measurement put the flag's choice in these two call sites, not in the spec, so a spec-only change would have left both doors on UTF-16. This is the producer of the `RegExp` moving into the spec, not consumer-side tolerance.
- **`@objectstack/formula`**: no source change. `matchesFilterCondition` answers through `matchesLikePattern`.
- No `driver-sql` / `driver-turso` / `driver-sqlite-wasm` source change. Those faces are the oracle; they gain test files only, per the card's "pin the family cells on every face".

### Changed `describe()` text, verbatim (`LIKE_DESCRIPTION`, both copies)

Before:

> "_" matches exactly one character, and a backslash escapes the character after it

After:

> "_" matches exactly one character, and a character is one Unicode code point — an emoji or any other character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane is ONE "_", never two, as SQL LIKE counts it. A backslash escapes the character after it

No refusal text changed. `likePatternToRegExp` throws the same plain `Error` as the source translation on a dangling escape (the backstop behind `hasDanglingLikeEscape`), and that message is pinned.

## Measured: every face, before and after

A probe (18 patterns over 9 values holding U+1F600 and U+1D49C) ran each face from its built `dist/` against a code-point oracle (the spec regex compiled with `u`):

| tree | spec `matchesLikePattern` | `formula` | memory `$like` door | memory AST door | better-sqlite3 | sql.js | Turso local | Turso remote (real libSQL) | differing cells |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base `e7f69dbb` | 12 differ | 12 differ | 12 differ | 12 differ | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | **48** |
| head `713d1504` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | **0** |

The driver-memory reference matcher is not exported from `dist/`, so it is pinned in the unit suite instead.

### The family cells, before → after on the JS faces (after = what every SQLite face already answered)

Rows: `x`, `😀`, `😀😀`, `a😀b`, `a😀😀b`, `A𝒜B`, `ab`, `axb`, `axyb`.

| op · pattern | before (UTF-16) | after (code point) |
|---|---|---|
| `$like` `_` | `x` | `😀`, `x` |
| `$like` `__` | `ab`, `😀` | `ab`, `😀😀` |
| `$like` `a_b` | `axb` | `a😀b`, `axb` |
| `$like` `a__b` | `a😀b`, `axyb` | `a😀😀b`, `axyb` |
| `$like` `___` | `axb` | `a😀b`, `axb`, `A𝒜B` |
| `$like` `😀_` / `_😀` | none | `😀😀` |
| `$ilike` `_` | `x` | `😀`, `x` |
| `$ilike` `A_B` | `axb` | `a😀b`, `axb`, `A𝒜B` |
| `$ilike` `A__B` | `a😀b`, `axyb`, `A𝒜B` | `a😀😀b`, `axyb` |

The answer set moves both ways, so the changeset's declaration names the measured direction arm, narrowing (BREAKING, graded `minor` in the launch window), with an ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` disposition. No pattern is newly refused, no refusal is lifted, and values made only of BMP characters answer exactly as before.

### Every consumer of the translation (Zone 2 item 2), before → after

| consumer | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `spec` `matchesLikePattern` | flagless `new RegExp`: UTF-16 | `likePatternToRegExp`: code point |
| `formula` `matchesFilterCondition` | via `matchesLikePattern`: UTF-16 | code point |
| `driver-memory` `$like` / `$ilike` door (mingo) | local flagless `new RegExp`: UTF-16 | `likePatternToRegExp`: code point |
| `driver-memory` AST `like` / `ilike` door (mingo) | local flagless `new RegExp`: UTF-16 | `likePatternToRegExp`: code point |
| `driver-memory` reference matcher | via `matchesLikePattern`: UTF-16 | code point |
| `driver-turso` `turso-20024-like-stored-nul` grid oracle | `matchesLikePattern`; its rows are BMP-only | unchanged answers |
| `service-analytics`, `@objectstack/lint`, objectql `having`, `driver-mongodb` | no consumer (`git grep` of both symbols) | none |
| objectui | `git grep` of both symbols: 0 hits at HEAD `5c61e5241` and at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `f8a9d0fb` (exit 1 on both; a control grep in the same tree hits) | none |

No other LIKE-to-regex translation exists in `packages/**/src`.

## `u`-flag side effects (Zone 2 items 3 and 4)

- **Escapes.** The translation escapes exactly `\ ^ $ . * + ? ( ) [ ] { } |` and `/`. That is the regex syntax characters plus `/`, exactly the identity escapes `u` accepts. Every other ASCII punctuation mark is emitted bare, where `u` reads it as itself. This is pinned over **all 33** printable ASCII non-alphanumerics, bare and backslash-escaped, with `foldAscii` off and on: each compiles under `u` and matches only itself. The escaped set is pinned to equal that set. A control proves `u` really rejects `\-` and `\:`.
- **`[\s\S]`, never `.`.** Both wildcards use `[\s\S]`, so under `u` a `_` is one code point including a newline (pinned: source `^[\s\S]$`, and `a_b` matches `a` newline `b`).
- **Surrogate pairs.** A character outside the BMP, literal or escaped, is emitted as its whole pair (pinned: the source for backslash + `😀` is `^😀$`), and `u` reads the pair as one code point. Under `u`, `%` never splits a pair: `%` followed by a lone low surrogate does not match `😀` (pinned).
- **`$ilike` / `foldAscii`.** The fold stays in the source as `[Aa]` classes, unaffected by `u`. `likePatternToRegExp(...).flags` is pinned to exactly `u`, with no `i`. The `$ilike` family cells are pinned on every face.

## The stop condition: nothing needs the UTF-16 reading (Zone 2 item 5)

- Nothing in `@objectstack/formula` lowers CEL to `$like`: `cel-to-filter` emits no `$like`, and `rls-predicate` leaves SQL `LIKE` unparseable. The only `$like` evaluation is `matches-filter.ts`, via the spec.
- CEL's own `size()` in `formula` already counts **code points**: `size('😀')` is 1 and `size('a😀b')` is 3 (pinned in the formula suite). The old `$like` answer disagreed with the same package's string length.

## Pins (every face, literal code-point rows, not parity alone)

| face | suite | cases |
|---|---|---|
| spec | `packages/spec/src/data/filter-like-code-point.test.ts` | 23 |
| formula | `packages/formula/src/matches-filter-like-code-point.test.ts` | 12 |
| driver-memory, all three doors | `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-20143-like-code-point.test.ts` | 11 |
| driver-sql (better-sqlite3) | `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-20143-like-code-point.test.ts` | 12 |
| driver-sqlite-wasm (sql.js) | `packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/sqlite-wasm-20143-like-code-point.test.ts` | 12 |
| driver-turso (local, remote stub, remote real libSQL) | `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-20143-like-code-point.test.ts` | 12 |

Each SQLite face also holds itself to the JS answer (`formula`, or the spec's `matchesLikePattern` where `formula` is not a dependency), which is the cross-face half.

## Ablation (committed fix first; one-shot, no permanent test file)

The mutation replaced the `'u'` flag argument with an expression that evaluates to the empty flag string and carries the marker `ABLATION20143`. It went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` under its restore trap, inside a script with its own `trap` restoring from `HEAD`.

- **Mutate leg:** on disk, marker count 1 and anchor count 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` exited 0, and `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs @objectstack/spec ABLATION20143` exited 0, so the marker is in `dist/`. The expected direction was written down before running: JS faces red on the family cells; SQLite faces green on their literal cells and red only on the cross-face leg. Observed: spec **13 failed** / 23; formula **11** / 12 (CEL `size()` stays green); driver-memory **10** / 11; driver-sql **1** / 12, driver-sqlite-wasm **1** / 12, driver-turso **1** / 12 (each the cross-face leg only). That is the predicted direction.
- **Restore leg:** `git hash-object` equals the `HEAD` blob `838a80720b3d`, `git diff HEAD` is empty, and `git status --porcelain` is clean. Rebuild exited 0, `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs ... --absent` exited 0, and all six suites are green again.

## Verification (at `713d1504`, after merging `origin/main` at `585c9af5`)

- Build of the six-package closure: turbo 10/10. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` passed after the merge. Regenerated here: `api-surface/data.json` (**0 breaking, 1 added**: `likePatternToRegExp`), `export-origins/data.json`, `content/docs/references/data/filter.mdx`.
- Full suites: spec 542 files / 15,943 passed (2 todo); formula 38 / 1,039; driver-memory 55 / 1,339; driver-sqlite-wasm 35 / 656; driver-turso 73 / 1,921 (16 skipped); driver-sql 189 files (+11 skipped) / 3,111 passed (170 skipped).
- Typecheck, exit 0 on all six: spec, formula, driver-memory, driver-sql, driver-sqlite-wasm, driver-turso. Each new test file is counted inside a compiled program with `--listFiles`: `tsconfig.json` for the four drivers, and `tsconfig.test.json` (via `check:test-typecheck`) for spec and formula.
- Gates: 108 derived at `713d1504` (`dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`), reconciled with `--ran`: **101 exit 0, 0 unrun, 7 NOT MEASURED**. All seven are exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET:
  - `check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:doc-security-posture` and `check:docs-transcript-drift` need `@objectstack/lint` built.
  - `check:lean-entry-closure` needs `objectql` built, and `check:skill-examples` needs `client` / `client-react` built.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` need the whole workspace built.

  The targeted prerequisite build never acquired the shared verify-lock (two 9-minute queue-timeouts behind other seats' batches), so those seven are declared to CI's Lint & Repo Gates. The seven roster families whose roster sits in a touched directory were run as well, all exit 0: `check:meta-url-spelling`, `check:spec-changes`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`, `check:object-def-param-keys`, `check:tenant-chokepoint`. `check-adr-0087-registration` reads the changeset as `[clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.

## Acceptance notes

- Three hand-written surfaces restate "`_` is exactly one character": `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx:553`, `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx:148`, and the `packages/client/src/query-builder.ts:88` JSDoc. They stay true under the reading the spec now defines, and are not edited here. Carrier: none.
- `likePatternToRegexSource` stays exported, so a future consumer could still compile it without `u`. Its docblock carries the prohibition, and after this PR nothing outside the spec calls it. Retiring the export would be a removal and is not this card.
- A value or pattern holding an unpaired surrogate is not measured. UTF-8 SQLite cannot store one, and the JS faces under `u` treat it as its own code point.
- The Postgres and MySQL `_` arms are NOT MEASURED, as on the card. SQL `_` is one character there.
